clue.text: Notes going up or down, doubly good in opera I arranged

indicators.note: things arranged are put into a new order, so the letters before it are reordered

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good, written twice

explanation.surface: A singer's run of notes, sung with double the goodness in an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: An arpeggio is a chord played as a sequence of single notes, rising or falling in turn.

clue.text: He's confused, he's disorganised — that's unbelievable!

indicators.note: a confused thing is muddled, so the first word's letters are mixed up
something disorganised is out of order, so the second word's letters are mixed up too

explanation.surface: Someone exasperated at a man who is muddled and disorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: The same three letters are scrambled twice, in two different ways, fitting the puzzle's theme of doubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheesh is an interjection voicing disbelief or exasperation, the kind of exclamation that greets something incredible.

clue.text: For no apparent reason, outlier upset over second conclusion he reaches

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the clue phrase is adverbial, describing a hidden motive

indicators.note: in a down clue one part placed over another comes first, on top of the rest
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the word before it is rearranged

parts.note: 'he' is the outlier, and its conclusion, its final letter, is reached a second time

explanation.surface: Someone puzzled why an odd one out is upset about a second verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: The R is the outlier's last letter used once more: the shuffled word keeps its own R, and gets a second one at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulterior motive is one kept hidden, so its reason is not apparent on the surface.

clue.text: Dual sign, for example, put up on car

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on another sits above it, so comes first
in a down clue, putting something up means writing it from bottom to top

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: An example of a two-way sign mounted on a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the Twins, is the zodiac sign whose symbol is a pair, so it is a dual sign.

clue.text: What do twins have close together? Places for sleeping, say

definitions.text: What do twins have close together?

indicators.note: 'say' asks us to speak the word, so what matters is how it is pronounced

parts.note: berths are bunks on a ship or train

explanation.surface: A riddle about twins, then bunk beds as the reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Twins are delivered within minutes of each other, so their arrivals are close together.
explanation.definitionFit: Twins are born at almost the same time, so their deliveries happen in close succession.

clue.text: Captain's position in game that features doubles

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the raised platform from which a ship is commanded
second meaning: the card game, in which a player may double an opponent's bid

explanation.surface: A sports captain's place in a game with doubles matches.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's captain stands on the bridge, and in the card game of that name 'double' is a standard call.

clue.text: Act duplicitously when selling coat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to overcharge or swindle a customer
second meaning: a sheep's wool, or a warm jacket

explanation.surface: A dishonest shopkeeper cheating a buyer over a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: To rob a buyer by overcharging is slang for skinning them, and a sheep's woolly coat shares the same word.

clue.text: Part of anxiety one reproduced?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the middle letters XI of anxiety are the Roman numeral for this number
second meaning: the digit 1 written twice makes 11

explanation.surface: A worried question about whether some element of anxiety is being copied.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves point at the number 11, once in Roman numerals tucked inside a word and once as a doubled digit.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven is written XI in Roman numerals and 11 in figures, a 1 repeated.

clue.text: Wounded slob stupidly extends risky commitment

indicators.note: doing something stupidly means doing it without order or sense, so the words before it are muddled

explanation.surface: An injured layabout foolishly takes on an even bigger gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: To double down is to increase a bet or commitment that is already risky, originally a blackjack move.

clue.text: This creed's delightful with both ends repeated

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective naming the creed; 'This creed' is a noun phrase

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word just found, said once more

explanation.surface: Praise for a creed that circles back to repeat its beginning and end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nicene Creed is the Christian statement of faith drawn up at the Council of Nicaea.

clue.text: Biased, not two-faced?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: partial, favouring one view
second meaning, read literally: having just a single face

explanation.walkthrough: Two-faced usually means hypocritical; here it is taken literally, and the opposite of having two faces is having one.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-sided argument is partial and prejudiced, and a thing with one side has only a single face.

clue.text: Biblical king was just a joke

explanation.surface: Dismissing an Old Testament ruler as nothing more than a laughing stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Agag was the Amalekite king spared by Saul and then killed by Samuel in the First Book of Samuel.

clue.text: Oddly, heirs did, by inheriting from different sources?

indicators.note: acting oddly means behaving strangely, so the words that follow come out in a strange order

explanation.surface: Heirs strangely acquired their fortunes from several separate relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is part of the scrambled letters, not a link; the definition is a whimsical take on crossbreeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybridised plant or animal is crossbred, getting its genes from two distinct parent stocks.

clue.text: Take ferry both ways, say, to do some selling down the river

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: go across a stretch of water twice

definitions.text: do some selling down the river
definitions.meaning: second meaning: betray someone who trusted you

explanation.surface: A trader takes the ferry there and back to sell goods downstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Selling down the river' is an idiom for betrayal, so the river and ferry are a shared false scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To double-cross is to betray an ally, just as selling someone down the river means betraying them.

clue.text: Noisy reaction and ferment heard, then repetitive laughter

indicators.note: something heard is taken in by the ear, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: to brew is to ferment, as beer does
a laugh written as a repeated syllable

explanation.surface: A rowdy response to fermentation, followed by guffawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy fuss or uproar, an outcry in reaction to something.

clue.text: Like certain images, being rude in a way

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as in '... image', an exact likeness
second meaning: ejecting saliva, a rude act

explanation.surface: Some pictures look as if they're being offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: A spitting image is an exact double of someone, tying this to the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'spitting image' describes a perfect likeness, and spitting at people is a coarse insult.

clue.text: Resembling stone from litchi caught dropping twice

indicators.note: the letter is dropped out of its place and lowered two steps, which in a down clue means further down the column

parts.note: an alternative spelling of lychee, the fruit
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A fruit's stony seed falls out twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The C of the fruit name moves two places down the light, ending up at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithic comes from the Greek for stone and describes things made of or like rock.

clue.text: Again consuming mushroom for muscle

indicators.note: something consuming another swallows it, so it wraps round it

parts.note: bis is a musical direction or encore call meaning twice, or again
a cep is the porcini mushroom

explanation.surface: Eating mushrooms again to build up muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: The biceps is the large muscle at the front of the upper arm, the one flexed to show strength.

clue.text: Humour very hard senior person who won't give up

parts.note: H is hard, as on a pencil; HH is doubly hard

explanation.surface: A very tough older person who refuses to surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Senior person' looks like one unit, but 'senior' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A withholder keeps something back, refusing to hand over what is asked of them.

clue.text: Vulgar laughter warmonger mostly echoed

indicators.note: an echo repeats a sound, so the shortened word is written twice
mostly means most but not all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a hawk is someone who favours war

explanation.surface: A war-loving politician's coarse guffaw echoes round the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Haw-haw imitates a loud, crude laugh, the braying sound of uncouth mirth.

clue.text: Double person making call

definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone who rings, by phone or on a bell

explanation.surface: A lookalike who makes a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead ringer is an exact lookalike, and anyone who rings a bell or a phone number rings.

clue.text: River goddess

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford
second meaning: the Egyptian mother goddess

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is itself a short word doubled, fitting the theme; the Thames at Oxford is traditionally called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper Thames near Oxford bears the Egyptian goddess's name, wife of Osiris.

clue.text: Asian dog food replicated

parts.note: replicated means copied, so the same word is set down a second time

explanation.surface: Dog food made in an Asian style is copied.
explanation.definitionFit: The chow chow is a sturdy Chinese breed with a lion-like mane and a blue-black tongue.

clue.text: Require to incorporate double time as scored

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take something into the body, so one part goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A worker needs overtime pay at double rate for the goals scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To net a goal is to score it, so a goal netted has been scored.

clue.text: Repeatedly taps a dance

parts.note: taps are marked C and H, for cold and hot
the three letters just built, written a second time

explanation.surface: Tapping again and again as one dances.
explanation.walkthrough: Taps here are the bathroom kind, labelled with letters for cold and hot.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha is a lively Latin American ballroom dance with a quick triple step.

clue.text: It includes doubles group outside pub sent back

indicators.note: sending something back makes it travel the other way, so the whole is read right to left
one thing outside another surrounds it, so it goes round the pub word

explanation.surface: A group drinking outside a pub gets sent away.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis has doubles matches, two players a side, alongside singles.
